Toyota is the major shareholder in a company called AISIN, a manufacturer of automotive components. Both companies are aware that cars are increasingly reliant on tech like image recognition, and that robotics and other forms of “physical AI” will need parts that overlap with cars. AISIN thinks existing chips aren’t a good fit for such roles, because they rely on external memory to store AI models and then generate a lot of traffic between a processor and the model. That traffic, the company contends, makes image recognition and other on-device uses of AI less effective. DRAM is also currently vastly expensive. The company’s response is a system-on-chip built on a 16nm FinFET process, an Arm Cortex A53 dual-core CPU, plus an Arm MaliG31 GPU. The chip includes built-in STT-MRAM, which stores both model weights and an operating system. AISIN and its research partners at Tohoku University say that approach means the chip can go from power-on to kernel startup in 65.7 milliseconds – 38 times faster than is possible if using external memory – and run the Tiny YOLOv3 object detection algorithm on the chip. “To effectively utilize the limited on-chip memory capacity, a hybrid multiplication architecture combining 8-bit and 16-bit multiplication was developed” according to a machine translation of Tohoku University’s announcement [PDF]. “By combining 16x16, 16x8, and 8x8 bit multiplication, the amount of weight data for the AI model was reduced by 53 percent, from 17.7MB to 9.36MB, while maintaining 16-bit precision.” AISIN is an established parts supplier and already sells to Toyota and other automakers but hasn’t said if or when it can get this chip into production. events.title: EQT seeks joint AI and data centre deals with Saudi and UAE sovereign investors
events.summary: EQT , Europe’s biggest private markets investment firm, is in talks with sovereign investors in the UAE and Saudi Arabia to explore joint artificial intelligence and infrastructure investment opportunities in the Arab world’s top two economies, its global chair has said. The company with $400 billion in assets, which has been raising funds from Gulf investors for decades, is keen to now deploy capital in the region , home to some of the biggest sovereign wealth funds in the world, Jean Eric Salata, told The National . “Here [in the UAE] I would say, and we've also been talking to Saudis as well, looking at opportunities there. Those are the two big areas that we're working on right now,” Mr Salata said of the continuing AI co-investment conversations with sovereign investors. “We're most excited about, which I think aligns with the strategic goals of the UAE, is the whole infrastructure, particularly data infrastructure and data centres, where we have globally one of the largest footprints.” The Stockholm private equity company plans to expand its AI infrastructure footprint in the Gulf through its portfolio firm EdgeConneX, which owns more than 106 data centres across 25 countries, he said. AI opportunity EQT, which currently manages more than $100 billion in digital and energy assets across markets, is the latest global investor looking to the rapidly developing AI and digital infrastructure sector in the region. AI has become a central plank of economic diversification efforts of the oil-rich Gulf economies that have already announced mega AI infrastructure projects. The UAE is leading the way with a planned five-gigawatt UAE-US AI campus in Abu Dhabi, which includes Stargate UAE – a massive 1GW computing cluster anchored by a $20 billion data centre investment. UAE Tech investors Khazna and G42 are working on these projects alongside global leaders such as OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia and Cisco, and investors such as SoftBank. Saudi Arabia, the largest Arab economy, has rolled out Project Transcendence, a $100 billion scheme to scale domestic AI and data infrastructure. The kingdom’s $1 trillion Public Investment Fund has also set up Humain to build out national cloud infrastructure in the country. Qatar’s sovereign arm, the Qatar Investment Authority, has also launched Qai, a $20 billion AI infrastructure partnership, to build out domestic GPU and data centre footprints. Since last year the three Gulf states have announced AI investment plans worth $120 billion, which exceeded 5 per cent of their gross domestic product, according to International Monetary Fund estimates. The sheer scale of investment required for AI development and data centres creates a huge opportunity for global investors such as EQT. The $1.3 trillion Blackstone Group has already struck a $3 billion deal with Saudi Arabia’s Humain, while tech giant Microsoft has committed over $10 billion towards data centres and related infrastructure across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait through to 2030. “There are many conversations that are ongoing right now with potential partners, both here [in the UAE] and elsewhere in the region,” Mr Salata said. “This is a sector that is capital constrained and is really, if you think about the AI build-out, the core, the key constraint in building the infrastructure is actually physical. It's the physical constraint around chips, energy, and data centres.” There is no shortage of demand for compute, hence a very strong investment case for building the power generation capacity and rolling out data infrastructure, he said. “I think that's where a lot of investment opportunity is right now for providers of long-term capital that can invest on a 15-year investment horizon,” he said. UAE SWF partnerships EQT opened an office in Abu Dhabi’s ADGM in September, joining the roster of trillion-dollar investors and asset managers including BlackRock, State Street, Blackstone Group, PGIM , Nuveen and Capital Group . A base in Abu Dhabi gives global investors opportunities to expand in the region and work closely with sovereign funds, large family offices and institutional partners. EQT is already working closely with the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, and Mr Salata said the firm is keen to expand that relationship. “They are one of our most important partners, and we're very excited to be working with them in, I would say, ever-increasing dimensions. We not only manage investments for Adia in our funds, but we also do a lot of co-investing together,” Mr Salata said. Adia is one of EQT’s largest co-underwriters in some of the European firm’s largest deals to take companies private in Europe. In June, Adia, along with Abu Dhabi’s $385 billion sovereign investment arm Mubadala Development Company, joined EQT’s £9.5 billion acquisition bid for the UK’s Intertek Group. Over the years, EQT has executed several co-investment deals with Mubadala, including the 2022 acquisition of Envirotainer, a biopharmaceutical industry solutions company. In 2025, Mubadala took a $600 million stake in Nord Anglia Education, and has been “a significant partner of ours all over the world”, he said. Deeping ties Establishing its first Middle East office in Abu Dhabi, Mr Salata said, was necessary to deepen its ties to the region, where it has active relationships with “many of the other sovereign wealth funds”. “The plan is to continue to develop those relationships regionally and use this office as a base to access them on a more regular basis,” he said. Forty EQT portfolio companies already have a presence in the Gulf, and with a local footprint, it expects more investments from regional sovereign investors to flow into those companies. “The logical place for us to start is with our existing portfolio companies,” Mr Salata said. “We really want to try and figure out how we can become more deeply involved in the investment ecosystem here,” he said. Over time EQT plans to bring more of its portfolio companies to the Gulf, and Mr Salata believes that the number will grow two or three-fold over the five to 10-year horizon. The sectors it seeks to invest in are “very much aligned with some of the longer-term trends in the region”, including infrastructure, education and health care, as well as technology and energy, where “the government policy is supportive”, he added.

events.title: Frantic Binance hackers created windfall for crypto traders
events.summary: Blockchain data firm Bitquery estimates the attackers lost about US$119 million through poor execution in their haste. Binance was hacked for US$6.3 billion, and North Korean hackers rushed to move stolen funds before stablecoins were frozen and withdrawals were halted. Their panic created sharp price gaps in Ether, TRX and other tokens, letting fast traders and bots make big profits from the chaos. Bitquery said hackers lost about US$119 million through poor execution, while Binance later restored withdrawals and said it had frozen about US$3 billion in affected assets. SAN FRANCISCO – For most crypto investors, the theft of US$6.3 billion (S$8.07 billion) from Binance was a reminder of the risks that still surround digital assets. For a small group of fast-moving trading firms and skilled investors, it was a chance to make a quick buck. As apparent North Korean hackers rushed to convert funds stolen from the world’s biggest crypto exchange, they accepted punishing prices. That handed well-prepared traders a fleeting but lucrative opportunity. Bitquery, a blockchain data firm, estimates the attackers lost about US$119 million through poor execution in their haste. “The hack created sharp price volatility and a single, large, price-insensitive seller moving through thin liquidity,” said James Aitchison, chief investment officer at Caerus Global Management. That aggressive, one-way torrent distorted crypto prices across disparate venues and blockchains, he said, adding: “We traded the event and found several attractive dislocations.” After gaining control of Binance funds on Oct 29, the attackers focused on getting rid of the stablecoin portion of the haul, knowing issuers would soon begin freezing those stolen tokens. Within roughly half an hour, they began aggressively swapping stablecoins such as USDT into other cryptocurrencies like Ether, which cannot be frozen, buying the tokens wherever they could and jacking up the price. Tether and Circle froze roughly US$1.8 billion worth of their stablecoins about 40 minutes after the main Ethereum leg of the hack began, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. Binance, meanwhile, stopped withdrawals while it investigated the breach. That disrupted the usual flow of money between trading venues and allowed price gaps that normally disappear in seconds to remain open far longer. Luca Parlamento, founder and chief investment officer of D2 Finance, said his firm spent the night “on the other side of the thief’s trades”. Parlamento said the attackers paid an average of about US$2,657 for Ether through decentralised exchanges such as Uniswap, well above the roughly US$2,300 price on Hyperliquid, a crypto derivatives platform. “The gap was ours to close,” Parlamento said. For traders with funds already sitting on such venues, the basic trade was straightforward: sell Ether where the hackers’ frantic buying had pushed the price unusually high and buy it where the price remained lower. Annanay Kapila, a former quant trader who runs derivatives exchange QFEX, was working in his central London office on the night of Oct 29 when he noticed that the price of Ether had skyrocketed on decentralised exchanges, reaching over US$3,000 in some cases. Kapila began to borrow large amounts of Ether on decentralised lending platform Aave, depositing stablecoins in return. He then sold his Ether on exchanges where its price was highest. Kapila said he made a 25% profit on the trades within five minutes. Crypto’s lack of persistent volatility in recent years means this kind of window is increasingly uncommon, Kapila said, with the last such event being when prices collapsed in October 2025. “Crypto’s been a little bit dead this year. Anytime there’s big dislocation, there are big opportunities,” Kapila said. “I’ve been around since 2021 where this was almost a weekly occurrence, stuff like this. But nowadays, it’s relatively rare.” The scale of the price gap showed the extent to which crypto’s typical market structure had been weakened. Achieving a fair price usually depends on traders being able to move coins quickly from one venue to another. Binance’s suspension of withdrawals also did not help, with locked funds preventing more traders from cashing in on the opportunity. The dislocations spread quickly to other tokens. One of the largest appeared on Tron, another blockchain network. Aitchison said the attackers swapped about US$234 million of USDT for 638 million TRX, Tron’s native token, in 16 trades. The average purchase price on a small venue called SunSwap was about 36.7 US cents, compared with a wider market price near 33 US cents. The buying briefly pushed the main trading pool as much as 18% above the broader market, and the gap took roughly 10 hours to fully disappear, he said.

events.title: Christmas 2026 stamps unveiled by Royal Mail
events.summary: Two stamps from the Royal Mail's annual Christmas collection Published 3 November 2026, 02:27 GMT Royal Mail has unveiled its Christmas stamps for this year - featuring scenes from the Nativity. The series of five stamps have been jointly created by graphic designer Gareth Howat and illustrator Rebecca Sutherland. The stamps depict familiar scenes of Mary and Joseph travelling, baby Jesus, an angel, the shepherds and the Three Wise Men. This year's collection marks the 60th anniversary of the first-ever Christmas special stamp. Sutherland said it was an "absolute honour" to be given the opportunity to illustrate the Christmas stamps for the Royal Mail. She said she has loved stamps since she was a child and had even collected them. "Being asked to create a set myself feels incredibly special," she added. The Christmas stamps from recent years have featured snowy scenes of UK cathedrals, or lyrics from famous carols - although 2025 also showed scenes from the Nativity. The first Christmas stamp collection came out in December 1966 after a children's art competition was announced by the then-postmaster Tony Benn. David Gold, of Royal Mail, said: "We hope this year's Christmas stamps will add an extra touch of festive magic to the millions of greetings sent to family and friends at home and around the world." events.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
events.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user’s Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines. A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said Google has severed ties with Videostrong Technology Co. , a TV box manufacturer in China that GTIG and other industry experts concluded was responsible for including malware that enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet dubbed “ XCPE ” (named after one of the malware’s core code components). The global distribution of XCPE botnet infections. Image: Google Threat Intelligence Group. The report said the XCPE botnet loaded the user’s device with software that makes their Internet address available for resale by multiple “residential proxy” services, which allow customers to rent Internet addresses as a way to anonymize their web traffic or spoof their true location. As detailed in several stories here over the past year , residential proxy services are a major source of unwanted and often malicious traffic, including account takeover activity, advertising fraud, and mass content scraping for AI projects. “Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices,” the GTIG post reads, noting that Google took legal action to take down the domains and servers Videostrong used to control the botnet and install additional malware. “A device manufacturer intentionally infecting their users with malware is an unacceptable breach of trust, and represents a serious risk to those users. Without users’ knowledge or consent, infected devices were offered as a distribution mechanism for a wide array of criminal actors.” The report notes that while TV boxes made up the the majority of the botnet, the same XCPE malware was found in other Android-based IoT products, including telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and even digital signage systems . Google said it requires all Android device makers to pass compatibility and security tests to ensure their products don’t harm users, but that Videostrong nevertheless found a way to load their malicious software immediately after a user boots up one of these devices for the first time (Google says it has since addressed that weakness). The GTIG report calls out a number of residential proxy providers whose software development kits were routinely downloaded by devices infected by the XCPE botnet. Those include AppSalt , also known as Honeygain , which is owned by the Vilnius, Lithuania-based Oxylabs . In October 2026, Oxylabs was relaunched under a new brand called Source , after receiving $130 million in funding from private equity firm Warburg Pincus that reportedly valued the business at $3.6 billion. Oxylabs did not respond to a request for comment. Another provider linked to the botnet was NetNut , a once sprawling residential proxy company operated by the publicly-traded Israeli company Alarum Technologies . In July 2026, the FBI worked with industry partners to seize hundreds of domains associated with NetNut , saying the company was responsible for operating a separate botnet called Popa that enslaved TV boxes as residential proxies. Other proxy providers named in the GTIG report include EarnFM , Traffmonetizer , Jaguar , LINKFOG , BMW/IPWeb and GaGaNode . Google’s announcement credits a number of industry partners, including Synthient , a startup that tracks proxy providers. In January 2026, Synthient published research into the rapid spread of the Kimwolf botnet, which at the time was hammering networks worldwide with record-smashing DDoS attacks . Synthient documented how Kimwolf infected millions of Android set-top boxes virtually overnight, using a widespread vulnerability in these residential proxy services to compromise other Android-based devices inside the local networks of unsuspecting TV box users. Synthient’s research caused dozens of residential proxy providers to patch their networks, which helped to fragment the Kimwolf botnet into much smaller pieces that made its incessant and disruptive DDoS attacks far easier for network operators to manage. It also attracted the attention of the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing the major Hollywood studios, which partnered with Synthient to purchase and tear apart a number of popular Android TV set-top boxes — including some that were being infected by Kimwolf and other IoT botnets. In a report published today, Synthient examined a popular, pre-infected TV box sold under the brand MECOOL by a publicly traded company in China called Skyworth Technology , concluding that MECOOL also bundled the malware from Videostrong Technology Co. and likewise installed AppSalt/Honeygain and other proxy components. The MECOOL storefront and marketing. Image: Synthient.com. Synthient founder Ben Brundage told KrebsOnSecurity that Videostrong’s malware also distributed software for the proxy service Grass . In our November 2025 story, “ Is Your Android TV Streaming Box Part of a Botnet? ” we quoted a researcher from Censys who found the popular Superbox TV streaming device bundled Grass’s residential proxy software. We also quoted the Grass founder, who denied any affiliation with the TV box maker. That November 2025 story noted that Superbox and similar Android TV set-top boxes gain new customers primarily by engaging influencers on Tiktok and other social networks who praise the product’s ability to offer hundreds of (pirated) pay TV streaming services for a one-time fee. Likewise, Synthient’s report observes that the MECOOL set-top boxes exploded in popularity after the product was mentioned in 2023 by the Youtube channel Linus Tech Tips, which has an audience of nearly 17 million subscribers [Linus Tech Tips said in a statement shared with Synthient that it has since updated the video to explicitly frame the product as a scam and have removed all associated affiliate links]. The popular Youtube channel Linus Tech Tips discussing MECOOL TV streaming boxes. events.title: HashKey Adopts Tokenised Deposit for Cross-Market Treasury and Liquidity Management on Standard Chartered's Blockchain Platform
events.summary: [The content of this article has been produced by our advertising partner.] Hong Kong, November 2, 2026 — HashKey Group (3887.HK), a leading Asian digital asset company, today announced that, its is among the first institutional clients to adopt Standard Chartered’s newly launched institutional tokenised deposit solution. HashKey is using the solution to support its institutional treasury management and settlement use cases. Tokenized deposits are the digital representations of commercial bank deposits on the blockchain. Built on Standard Chartered’s blockchain infrastructure, they enable eligible clients, such as HashKey to use their bank deposit balances within an approved blockchain-based environment, while retaining the characteristics of commercial bank money. By combining the trust of bank deposits with blockchain-enabled programmability, speed and extended availability, Standard Chartered’s tokenized deposits can facilitate near real-time movement of funds, and support more efficient cross-border liquidity management with extended availability. For HashKey, which operates across multiple jurisdictions, the ability to move liquidity across markets outside traditional banking hours is particularly important. While digital asset activity takes place around the clock, the movement of funds between HashKey’s entities has traditionally been constrained by banking cut-off times. Tokenised deposits help bridge this gap by enabling near real-time, extended-hours movement of funds, giving HashKey greater flexibility to manage treasury positions across markets and entities, reduce funding friction and deploy working capital more efficiently in support of its global operations. Haiyang Ru, CEO of the HashKey Exchange BG, stated: "As more assets move on-chain, fund and settlement systems also need to evolve synchronously. The significance of tokenized deposits lies in connecting funds within the banking system more directly to the on-chain environment. Being among the first institutional clients to adopt Standard Chartered’s newly launched tokenised deposit solution is an important step in strengthening HashKey’s institutional financial infrastructure. We look forward to exploring more efficient fund-flowing methods with global financial institutions, providing more comprehensive infrastructure support for institutions participating in on-chain finance." Mark Willis, Head of Emerging Payments, Transaction Services and Digital Assets, Standard Chartered, said: "Tokenised deposits can play an important role in connecting commercial bank money with the digital asset ecosystem, giving clients greater flexibility in how they move and manage liquidity across markets. Our work with HashKey demonstrates how this technology can support near real-time, extended-hours movement of funds, helping clients manage treasury and liquidity more efficiently while supporting their digital asset activities. This is about bringing the trust of bank deposits together with the speed and programmability of blockchain to solve real-world treasury needs." In recent years, HashKey has continuously promoted the construction of institutional-grade digital asset infrastructure, expanding its business network with its "Asia Interconnected" strategy, and deepening its business layout and financial connections in major Asian markets. Relying on the group's cross-jurisdiction compliant license layout, institutional customer service capabilities, and continuously expanding global financial institution partnership network, HashKey continues to expand channels for institutional funds to enter the digital asset market, enhancing cross-market capital management, trading, and settlement capabilities. Based on HashKey's long-term business experience in serving institutions and professional investors, HashKey will further improve its global treasury management capabilities, strengthen the infrastructure connection between the traditional financial system and the digital asset market, and provide more efficient fund-flowing support for tokenized assets and other on-chain financial applications. In the future, HashKey will continue to deepen cooperation with global financial institutions, explore the practical applications of tokenized deposits in institutional business, and promote the further connection between the traditional financial system and on-chain financial markets. HashKey Group（“HashKey”, the Company, Stock Code: 3887.HK） is a leading digital asset company in Asia with a global footprint, providing end-to-end financial infrastructure, technology and investment management to create a digital assets ecosystem. The Company offers a licensed digital asset platform to provide transaction facilitation services, on-chain services, and asset management services. We are a leading international banking group, with a presence in 55 of the world’s most dynamic markets.

events.title: Fox-Roku deal poised to clear Justice Department scrutiny under consent decree
events.summary: The Scoop Fox’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku is poised to clear Justice Department scrutiny and move forward under a consent decree, according to people familiar with the deliberations, despite efforts from a right-wing ally of President Donald Trump to hold up the deal. It’s unclear what a consent decree would entail, or what terms are being considered. It’s possible the DOJ could change course, the people said. Fox declined to comment. Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward also declined to comment on the deal. “However, we can affirm that this DOJ under President Trump’s leadership will continue to prioritize affordability for all Americans across our economy,” he said in a statement. The deal, which would unite Fox’s content empire of news and sports with Roku’s dominant connected-TV operating system, had worried rivals who fear that Fox will favor its own content. Roku’s free, ad-supported channel also competes for viewers and content with Tubi, which Fox owns. Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch has said his “expectation” is to run the two businesses separately while selling advertising across them. Semafor first reported in September that antitrust regulators were widening the inquiry into the deal, days before the two companies confirmed the deeper probe, known as a “second request.” That enhanced scrutiny came in part because of pressure from Newsmax majority owner Chris Ruddy, who bills himself as a Trump confidant and has had a long-running spat with Fox owner Rupert Murdoch, Semafor later reported. Rohan’s view Ruddy, briefly a reporter for Murdoch’s New York Post in the 1990s, has been feuding with Fox for more than a year over streaming access to his media assets. Murdoch’s camp has previously dismissed Newsmax’s efforts as a bid to “sue their way out of their own competitive failures,” and Murdoch himself has dined with Trump more than once. But it’s clear that Ruddy has been a headache for the Murdoch clan. Investors have fretted about the possibility that Fox’s deal for Roku could get tied up as a result of Ruddy’s efforts. Those worries were exacerbated after Fox ousted business anchor Maria Bartiromo following an internal investigation into allegations she leaked internal network information and communications to the Trump administration, a claim her lawyers have disputed. But if the deal goes through, it’s more evidence that the Murdoch name still carries a fair amount of weight in Washington.

events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts North Korea dismisses Binance heist allegations as 'absurd' US rhetoric Kim Jong Un is the leader of North Korea, which has been accused of orchestrating the largest crypto heist in history. ( KCNA via Reuters ) North Korea has denied FBI allegations accusing the country of stealing $US6.3 billion from crypto exchange platform Binance. Ruling party official Kim Yo Jong dismissed the allegations as "absurd rhetoric and nothing new" from the US. Binance customers have withdrawn $US4.64 billion after the company lifted a temporary suspension on withdrawals. North Korea has denied US allegations that it was behind the $US6.3 billion ($9 billion) heist of cryptocurrency exchange platform Binance as "absurd rhetoric" and proof that Washington remained hostile towards the country. In a statement published by North Korean state media, Kim Yo Jong , the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, denied the country was responsible for carrying out last week's hack, thought to be the largest financial heist in history. Who is behind world's largest crypto heist? Almost $9 billion in cryptocurrency was hacked from exchange company Binance, but who was behind the attack? Ms Kim also warned the country had "issues to reconsider" over US hostility. "The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state,' claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident," she said in the statement. "But the US assertion is absurd rhetoric and nothing new. "It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds." On Saturday, the FBI accused a North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor of carrying out the hack and stealing billions in crypto. The FBI says North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor is behind the heist. ( Pexels: Tibe De Kort ) The US bureau said it had observed TraderTraitor converting stolen assets into a cryptocurrency called Ethereum and expected it to launder the assets further. "The FBI maintains its commitment to protecting the virtual asset community by identifying, mitigating, and disrupting North Korea's illicit cybercrime and virtual asset theft activities," a statement read. Cybersecurity experts said North Korean hackers were among the world's most prolific crypto thieves, with the proceeds used to help fund the country's weapons programs. North Korea has denied all allegations of its links to cryptocurrency theft and other cybercrimes. Ms Kim said North Korea would reconsider unspecified issues in light of the "very unpleasant US hostile attitude". It comes as Pyongyang remains silent on US President Donald Trump's offers to resume US-North Korea summit diplomacy. Experts have indicated Pyongyang may be weighing its options. Binance customers withdrew about $US4.64 billion ($6.6 billion) worth of assets after the company lifted its temporary suspension on Sunday. Zhao Changpeng is the founder and CEO of Binance, which has moved to reassure its users following the hack. ( Reuters: Benoit Tessier ) "Between 06:00 and 15:30 UTC on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion," the company said on X. "Our team continues testing rigorously the remaining networks and assets. "Rest assured that market conditions are stable." The company said it had recovered 90 per cent of the stolen assets by using company money. ( ABC News: Fletch Yeung ) Iconic department store David Jones is being forced to defend its viability, as the Australian retailer faces speculation about store closures and misses a crucial filing deadline. The department store's key lender has already chipped in extra cash to allow David Jones to stock up before the busy festive season. Hilco Capital would not confirm the amount, but the ABC understands it is about $10 million. Do you know more? Email our journalist on terzon.emilia@abc.net.au or em.terzon@proton.me "Hilco remains supportive of the business and any inference otherwise is false," the lender said in a statement. The ABC has confirmed that David Jones just missed a deadline to file its most recent financial year reports to the corporate regulator, ASIC. Meanwhile, there is ongoing media speculation that the retailer is going to call it quits on several stores inside Westfield shopping centres. It currently has 38 stores nationally. David Jones is owned by private equity firm Anchorage Capital Partners. A spokesperson for that Australian firm said it would not comment on speculation. But the spokesperson noted David Jones was reviewing its store network and was in discussions with stakeholders to put itself "on a viable financial footing". David Jones's future is unclear. ( ABC News: Fletch Yeung ) A key union that represents retail workers, the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association (SDA), said it was reaching out to workers at David Jones informing them of their rights if the retailer went under. "The reports of David Jones' predicament are alarming," the SDA noted in a statement. It is understood at least one major fashion brand has pulled some of its stock from David Jones amid concerns the retailer could not pay its bills. Suppliers have also already been put on extended terms this year to give David Jones more time to pay for stock. David Jones was first founded as a corner shop in Australia in 1838 and today has multi-level department stores across Australia that sell everything from cosmetics to shoes and fashion. Its main rival is the ASX-listed Myer, which early last year voted to merge with Solomon Lew's apparel brands Just Jeans, Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti and Jacqui E . That merger was billed as a way for Myer to keep relevant in a changing retail landscape, where younger generations are increasingly shopping online or opting for second-hand apps such as Depop. events.title: Indonesia’s severe drought threatens to disrupt China’s vast battery industry
events.summary: A severe drought in Indonesia is slowing output of a crucial material used to make electric vehicle batteries A severe drought in Indonesia is slowing output of a crucial material used to manufacture electric vehicle (EV) batteries, creating risks across China’s vast electric car supply chain. Indonesia is a vital link in the global electric car supply chain. The Southeast Asian nation is the world’s biggest production hub for nickel, a metal that is converted into a component used in lithium-ion batteries. But a sharp drop in rainfall in the country is causing local nickel refineries to reduce output, a move that could “add uncertainty … across the battery materials value chain”, according to market analysis firm CRU Group.

events.title: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing…something with third-party AI apps
events.summary: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Apple’s services business remains at record levels, but it’s facing growing pressure . The central part of that business, Apple’s App Store, has faced regulatory pressure and a slump in mobile gaming, which have hurt services growth . However, on Monday’s earnings call, Apple signaled that it may look to boost services revenue through third-party apps. What does that mean, exactly? Unfortunately, it’s not entirely clear. When discussing how AI could potentially “contribute to revenue growth over time,” Kevan Parekh, Apple’s chief financial officer, said: “On the product side, you know, we feel AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities, and we also feel there’s opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities.” Parekh did not elaborate on what sorts of opportunities might be available via third-party apps. However, Reuters reported Monday that investors are wondering whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through the App Store and taking a cut of the revenue they generate. Regulatory and legal changes have cut into App Store commission revenue in some markets, even as Apple’s services business as a whole continues to grow. Third-party estimates in August, for example, suggested the company had seen an 18% drop in U.S. commission revenue, with declines also in Brazil and Japan after those countries introduced new regulations. Apple has traditionally controlled payments within its app marketplace tightly, taking a cut of all App Store transactions. But a lawsuit by Epic Games ultimately forced the company to allow apps to redirect users to outside payment systems. Other legal challenges throughout the world have further hampered the business. During the earnings call, Parekh referenced Apple’s App Store woes and returned to the idea that the company’s service business could expand into new territory. “We’ve also seen some factors that impacted the performance of the App Store, and during the September quarter, the performance on the App Store was similar to the prior year, and we had a record number of paid subscriptions with double-digit growth for third-party apps on the App Store,” Parekh said. “At the same time, we did see some headwinds in mobile gaming that we’ve talked about before, and expect to see those continue into the summer quarter.” Parekh added: “As we move ahead, we expect services growth to be between 8 to 9% [in the December quarter]. This outlook contemplates our best estimates on sequential headwinds, primarily from third-party licensing and the additional half percentage point of foreign exchange I just mentioned.” TechCrunch has reached out to Apple for more information and will update this story if it responds. events.title: Oil rises after report of US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island
events.summary: Earlier, US and Iran signalled that diplomatic talks are continuing. Oil prices rose after a Wall Street Journal report said the US struck Iran’s Qeshm Island, lifting fears of wider conflict and oil supply disruption. Brent crude rose 0.5% to US$105.25 and WTI rose 0.5% to US$96.93, after Brent had fallen 7.63% the day before. Tehran said talks with the US continue, while Trump said a deal may still happen and the US-Iran war keeps pressure on Strait of Hormuz traffic and petrol prices. Oil prices rose in early Asian trade on Nov 3 after a report that the US had struck Iran’s Qeshm Island, raising concerns about an escalation of the eight-month long conflict and prolonged disruptions to Middle East oil supplies. Brent crude futures rose 48 US cents, or 0.5%, to US$105.25 a barrel by 1.04am GMT (9.04am Singapore time), while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 47 US cents, or 0.5%, at US$96.93 a barrel. Brent crude futures settled US$8.66, or 7.63%, lower to US$104.77 a barrel on Nov 2. The United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials. Some of the officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. “The report added a degree of risk premium back into the oil price. Just when markets were starting to price in a more diplomatic path, this reminder of ongoing military activity has flipped the tone,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. Meanwhile, Tehran said on Nov 3 that contacts between Iran and the US to end their war are continuing, after days of Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough. Trump raised doubts on Nov 3 about whether he would follow through on a threatened resumption of military strikes against Iran and said a deal with Tehran could happen. The US-Iran conflict that began in late February has sharply reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which previously carried about a fifth of global crude oil and natural gas supplies. The Iran war is a leading cause of high petrol prices that are weighing on voters in the US ahead of the midterm elections on Nov 3, and Trump is under pressure to end the conflict. Brent ended October at its highest in six months on concerns that the Middle East conflict could escalate again after the vote. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government certain authorities for peace talks. Additionally, the US will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10 and 11 to discuss ending Moscow’s war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements and de-escalation. ( ABC News: Che Chorley ) Cleaning services LYLA has become the second company to have its contract suspended from the $15.4 billion Torrens to Darlington project. The SA government earlier confirmed the Torrens to Darlington Alliance, tasked with delivering the road corridor upgrade, had cancelled its contract with Career Boss on the grounds the company had not been "proactively disclosing" its involvement in a civil legal suit. State parliament's budget and finance committee has summoned the alliance to answer questions over its due diligence processes. A second company has been suspended from the Torrens to Darlington project, because of what the government says is a common shareholding with a labour hire firm that had its contract terminated amid a civil suit surrounding alleged bikie threats. The SA government said small cleaning subcontractor LYLA was not the subject of any allegations of criminal wrongdoing but had been "suspended from all work" on the $15.4 billion road corridor project. It said that step had been taken purely out of an "abundance of caution because of the common shareholding" with Career Boss, which has since had its contract terminated after it was suspended last month. A watered down ICAC gets called up for a full-bodied political scandal The government asking the state's anti-corruption watchdog to look at the $15.4 billion South Road project has been spun as a proactive step against potential bikie infiltration, but there is devil is in the detail. "Whether you have any link whatsoever to Career Boss, the message from the government is very clear: there is no place for you on the T2D, there is a zero-tolerance approach," Transport Minister Joe Szakacs said. On its website, LYLA Services lists an address at a Salisbury commercial building which is also home to Career Boss. The building has exterior signage for Career Boss, but LYLA Services is not publicly displayed. The ABC has sought a response from LYLA Services. The government said there was "no suggestion of wrongdoing by LYLA, its shareholders, directors, or owners". "This common shareholding of this company LYLA shows that we won't tolerate companies that have any association with anything that might be considered inappropriate for the North-South corridor," Treasurer Tom Koutsantonis said. "Sometimes, people will think this is unfair. We don't care. "There will be new tenders that go out and new companies will tender. There will always be an ongoing assessment of every single company that is working on this." Joe Szakacs says the government is taking "a zero-tolerance approach". ( ABC News: Che Chorley ) The government reiterated that SA Police last week had found "no evidence of organised crime on any public infrastructure project", including the T2D. Late last month, the SA premier wrote to SA's Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) requesting an evaluation of the Torrens to Darlington project. ICAC commissioner Emma Townsend later confirmed she was "independently of the view" it was in the public interest to evaluate the Department for Infrastructure and Transport's policies. Opposition leader Ashton Hurn said today's developments further demonstrated the need for a "forensic audit of every single contract". SA Opposition Leader Ashton Hurn has repeated a call for a forensic audit of contracts. ( ABC News: Che Chorley ) "Since day one, the government has not got its story straight on who knew what when," she said. "[It's] this type of absolute chaos that allowed billions of dollars in Victoria to flow to the very wrong people. We don't want to see that happen in South Australia." Labour hire company agreement torn up Mr Koutsantonis said the T2D Alliance, a consortium of companies selected to deliver the major infrastructure works, had the power to terminate contracts on the project. Earlier today, Premier Peter Malinauskas said Career Boss's contract on the T2D project has been terminated over its involvement in a civil suit surrounding alleged bikie threats. A labour hire company has had its previously suspended contract on the Torrens to Darlington project terminated. events.title: GOP's midterm blame game starts early
events.summary: Republicans don't know if they'll lose big or small on Tuesday, but they're already bracing for an epic blame game. Why it matters: Privately, Republicans acknowledge it's not a complicated version of Clue. The leading suspect: Mr. President , in the Oval Office, with an assortment of weapons — and one war. Returning Republican senators are unlikely to blame President Trump publicly. There's a price for that. And don't expect Trump to shoulder the responsibility. But do expect departing GOP lawmakers to take shots at Trump or his team, and Trump to fire back at Senate Republicans, whom he's never been shy about torching. The irony of Trump's second midterm: With Republicans privately resigned to losing the House, Trump can still credibly claim victory if they hold the Senate. "It's Donald Trump's midterms. He gets all the credit if we win. He gets all the credit if we lose," one national GOP strategist told Axios. The Iran war: From Alaska to Maine, Trump's decision to go to war with Iran — and the resulting spike in gas and diesel prices — has become a major political liability for Republican Senate nominees. "It's not tariffs … it's the war, it's gas prices, it's diesel," Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said at a closed-door fundraiser in September, Axios reported last month . Tariffs: Trump's trade policies have compounded Republicans' affordability problems, particularly in farm country, where producers have faced higher costs and uncertainty over export markets. "We need to end this tariff war now," former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) , the GOP Senate nominee, said in an October campaign ad, breaking with Trump over his tariffs on Canada. Bad candidates: Trump's preferred nominees are also drawing blame, GOP strategists tell Axios. Paxton in Texas and Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina have forced Republicans to spend heavily defending races that should have been easier — and where the party had other options. Complacent incumbents: Sens. Roger Marshall (R-Kan.) and Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.) are facing accusations of "arrogance" and "laziness" from Republicans frustrated that their once-safe seats have become late-breaking battlegrounds — exactly the complacency NRSC Chair Tim Scott warned against. Weak governors: Underperforming gubernatorial nominees in Iowa, Michigan and Ohio threaten to drag down Republican Senate candidates. Vivek Ramaswamy, for example, saw his polling crater in the final weeks . Recruitment failures: Republicans couldn't persuade Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp to run for Senate, and in New Hampshire settled for their second-choice Sununu — former Sen. John Sununu — instead of his brother, former Gov. Chris Sununu. Meanwhile, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) landed marquee candidates in Alaska, Ohio and Iowa — though Michigan and Maine proved more difficult. MAGA money: Trump's political operation amassed an enormous war chest, but some Republicans complain the money arrived too late to rescue vulnerable candidates. Distractions: Trump's focus on D.C. construction projects, the Kennedy Center, Sen. Jon Husted's (R-Ohio) backside and the SAVE Act has frustrated Republicans desperate for a closing message focused on the economy. "Reflecting Pool presser was an interesting choice for closing message," another national GOP strategist said of Trump's Monday news conference.

events.title: Dodge announces return to NASCAR Cup Series beginning at Daytona 500
events.summary: Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, a year earlier than initially expected LAS VEGAS -- Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, a year earlier than initially expected. The Stellantis-owned Dodge brand announced its return at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas on Monday. Dodge will once again give the Cup Series four manufacturers, joining Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota in fielding entries to compete in a 36-race schedule that begins in mid-February and crowns a champion in early November. Kaulig Racing will use the Dodge Charger to field a two-car team beginning at the Daytona 500. AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon are expected to fill those seats. “Dodge’s return to the NASCAR Cup Series is a significant milestone for the sport,” NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell said in a statement. “This commitment speaks to Dodge’s belief in our sport and gives fans another reason to be excited about what’s ahead. “The partnership between NASCAR, (Ram CEO) Tim Kuniskis and the entire team at Stellantis has been nothing short of phenomenal. They have a deep passion for NASCAR and its ability to showcase the world’s top brands, and we can’t wait to see Dodge on the racetrack for the Daytona 500 and beyond.” Dodge raced in NASCAR through the 2012 season and left the same month it celebrated the Cup title with Brad Keselowski and Penske Racing. It was Dodge’s first Cup championship since Richard Petty’s sixth of seven titles in 1975. Dodge re-entered the NASCAR Truck Series with its Ram brand in 2026, with eyes on expanding to the premier Cup Series in 2028. Kuniskis vowed to be disruptive while doing it “unlike anyone else.” Learjet with 9 aboard crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida: FAA Parents and 2 young children among victims of Learjet crash in Florida, family says 2 college students found dead after going missing while hiking, police say Kuniskis said Ram planned to tap into NASCAR’s estimated fan base of 20 million “and turn it into 80 or 100 million.” Kaulig had five trucks race this season, all of which are outside the top 10 in the series standings heading to the season finale at Homestead, Florida, this weekend. Normally, it would have taken Dodge two years to get ready for the Cup Series. But Dodge bypassed part of the timeline required to develop a new engine by partnering with Earnhardt Childress Racing to build Dodge-spec powerplants alongside its regular Chevrolet operations. Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota allowed that unique partnership in part because they believed a fourth manufacturer in NASCAR would be good for the overall health of the racing series. events.title: PBOC to raise banks’ forex reserve requirements to ease yuan appreciation pressure
events.summary: The People’s Bank of China says it will increase the reserve requirement ratio on foreign exchange deposits later this month The People’s Bank of China announced on Tuesday that it would raise the reserve requirement ratio on foreign exchange deposits by 2 percentage points. The ratio would be 6 per cent, effective November 15, the central bank said in a statement, calling it a move to strengthen the liquidity management of financial institutions. The policy, which would require banks to hold a larger share of their foreign currency deposits in reserve at the central bank, is expected to tighten onshore foreign-currency liquidity, potentially easing appreciation pressure on the yuan. The currency recently broke through the 6.65 per US dollar mark to reach its strongest level since June 2022.

Ukrainian drone teams have a new way to spy on the drones that spy on them. A Kyiv equipment startup called CODE380 has been gaining attention for a pocket-sized receiver, the D·Vision SDR, that picks up live camera video from many Russian drones and shows it on a screen. Those drones send their video over the air without any scrambling, so anyone with the right receiver can watch along. A Ukrainian unit can see where a drone is heading and what its pilot is aiming at before it hits. According to Defense News , the device is light, at about 10 ounces, which is less than half the weight of competing Ukrainian models, one of which weighs a couple of pounds. It also listens on the radio channels Russia’s newer Molniya drones started using for video in June. Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a radio specialist who advises Ukraine’s president, said in a June Facebook post cited by Defense News that “most detectors don’t see these frequencies, or see them poorly.” He warned that putting too much trust in a detector could prove fatal. Beskrestnov has also warned that digital video could one day replace analog, which would blind receivers like this one. The New York Times reported in August that some Molniyas are AI-guided, using Nvidia chips and emitting no signals . events.title: Asian stocks fall on US tech jitters and yuan weakens
events.summary: In a sign some investors are looking to buy on dips, US stock futures gained. Japan is closed for a holiday. Asian stocks fell as US chipmaker losses deepened and investors waited for the US midterm elections. South Korea’s Kospi dropped almost 4%, led by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. China’s market support steps failed to lift shares, with the CSI 300 down 0.1%. The renminbi ended 13 straight gains after the People’s Bank of China asked banks to hold more foreign currency reserves. Oil steadied after an 8% fall, while Apple shares slipped on a mixed outlook. Analysts said markets are in a “risk-off mood” because of AI worries, politics, and geopolitics. Asian stocks fell as a sell-off in US chipmakers deepened and investors grew reluctant to trade ahead of the US midterm elections. The MSCI Asia Pacific gauge dropped almost 1% with South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi Index sliding almost 4%. The decline came after a gauge of US chipmakers extended a three-day rout, bringing its losses to 12%. The Nasdaq 100 has declined 10% from its peak, entering a technical correction. Japanese markets were closed for a holiday. Chinese equities fell even after the central bank said it would encourage financial institutions to make greater use of stock-support tools and optimise their terms as the authorities seek to bolster market stability. The renminbi ended its longest winning streak in three decades after the People’s Bank of China moved to cool its rally by asking banks to hold more foreign currencies in reserve . The renminbi weakened as much as 0.4% to 6.6728 per dollar, halting 13 straight days of gains, which was the longest streak since 1996. Kieran Calder, head of Asia equity research at Union Bancaire Privee, said: “Markets are mostly in a risk-off mood against the background of increasing AI concerns and the US midterm elections . “We have looked at all US midterm elections since 1950 and found that the S&P 500 was higher six months later in each case. If this trend persists, we expect markets should move higher into year-end, but it could be a rocky week.” South Korea’s Kospi Index led declines in Asia, with shares of its two chip giants, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, dropping more than 4%. Hebe Chen, market analyst at Vantage Global Prime, said South Korea’s semiconductor-heavy market is “back on the front line of the global AI trade’s repricing”. “The divergence on Wall Street, where tech heavyweights are losing ground even as broader market breadth improves, suggests investors are rotating away from crowded AI trades rather than abandoning equities altogether.” Brent crude steadied after plunging almost 8% on Nov 2, as the US and Iran signalled a willingness to pursue peace talks as the war in the Middle East enters its ninth month . The global benchmark was near US$105 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate was below US$97 after its biggest decline in three months on Nov 2. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government had been granted more authority by the nation’s supreme leader to negotiate , while US President Donald Trump hinted at progress in talks. Still, simmering hostilities are keeping the market on edge. Apple’s shares fell in late US trading after the company delivered a mixed outlook to investors in its first quarterly report under chief executive John Ternus, with narrower profit margins overshadowing an upbeat sales forecast. Elsewhere, Anthropic disclosed a twelvefold rise in quarterly revenue while outlining plans to spend more than US$895 billion (S$1.15 trillion) in the coming years. China’s CSI 300 Index slipped 0.1% amid scepticism about the authorities’ latest market support measures. The two liquidity-injection tools – a swop facility and relending operations to encourage more stock purchases – reappeared with some adjustments as the authorities sought to bolster market stability and confidence. Chinese shares have been mired in a slump since the summer, weighed down by a weak economy and doubts over AI earnings. Previous attempts to revive the market – including a round of buying by the so-called national team starting in July, and regulatory guidance to curb selling in October – have fallen short. Elsewhere, a Bloomberg gauge of the dollar edged higher, while US Treasury 10-year futures fell 3/32. There was no trading of cash Treasuries in Asia owing to the holiday in Japan. Australia’s dollar fell after the central bank raised its key interest rate to an 18-year high, as economists forecast, in a split vote. The Aussie dropped as much as 0.5% to 69.99 US cents. US job openings data due on Nov 3 is expected to show that listings edged higher in September, while weekly jobless claims due on Nov 5 are seen remaining near historically low levels. Economists expect the Nov 6 payrolls report to show US job growth more than doubled to 65,000 in October, with the unemployment rate holding at 4.2%.

events.title: Disney eyes thousands of layoffs, with managers asked to target 20% in cost savings
events.summary: The 20% in annual cost savings could come from job eliminations as well as from expense reductions. Disney is planning thousands of job cuts, with some managers told to find 20% annual cost savings through layoffs and lower spending. Chief executive Josh D’Amaro wants to use some savings for film and TV content, technology, theme parks and cruise ships. The cuts follow years of cost reductions across Disney, as traditional TV weakens and streaming growth slows; Disney had 231,000 staff worldwide last year. BURBANK, California – Walt Disney is moving towards thousands of job cuts, with the entertainment giant asking some managers to target 20% in annual cost savings, according to sources familiar with the matter. The savings could come from job eliminations as well as from expense reductions, said the sources, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. Some of Disney’s operations, from theme parks to the TV network and the movie studio, will be affected disproportionately. Chief executive Josh D’Amaro aims to reinvest a portion of the savings into film and TV programming, technology, and the theme parks and cruise ship businesses, the sources said. The company has promised double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share in the current fiscal year. A representative for Disney declined to comment. Disney has cut billions of dollars worth of costs and eliminated thousands of positions in recent years, with reductions impacting every division including ABC, Pixar, ESPN, the film studio and the experiences unit. The company had 231,000 people worldwide at the end of the last fiscal year. The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct 1 that Disney was planning a restructuring of its TV division, and cuts at the company’s legal and global affairs unit. Other entertainment companies including Netflix, Sony Pictures Entertainment, and Skydance’s Paramount and Warner Bros. divisions have also cut jobs as revenue from traditional TV declines and streaming subscriber growth slows. They also have to cope with more viewers tuning to social media, online videos and streaming services backed by tech giants like Amazon.com and Apple. At the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles in October, Disney president Dana Walden said: “There is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured and how big is the organisation. “Technology set their sights on our business and we must survive and thrive and grow, and that’s what we’re going to do.” BLOOMBERG

Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan has, in the past, jokingly admitted that he’s suffered from “cyber psychosis” and sometimes barely sleeps because he’s so excited to be working with his AI agents. On a new episode of Walter Isaacson’s podcast The Builders , set to publish on Tuesday, Tan put a price tag on his passion. “I spend about maybe $100[,000] to $200,000 a year on tokens,” he told Isaacson. He uses agents for countless work projects and coding tasks and has freely shared his set of 23 Claude Code skills, called gstack , on GitHub — an effort to help teach others what agents can do, he said. On the one hand, he uses his agent the way many people use AI: to help him research Isaacson’s podcast and prep for the kinds of questions he might be asked. On the other, his agent also helps him run his life. “It’s read all of my email and all of my Dropbox. It’s read, like, all of my Apple Notes, even my therapy notes going back 20 years,” he said. He describes using AI agents as getting help with “almost anything that you do in your day-to-day life, and for it to do it somewhat more autonomously. Think of it as a Jiminy Cricket on your shoulder at all times. Like, almost anything you want to do, it knows you, and it’s there to help. And it will actually sort of run ahead and say, ‘What about this?’ Or it’ll help you see around corners.” As an early OpenClaw adopter who is now a power user, Tan says one thing he’s learned is not to treat AI agents like traditional software. Some people are so worried about “repeatability and safety that they actually trade off all of the beautiful parts of working with an AI agent, which basically can be so similar to a human,” he said. For instance, Y Combinator is also using an agent that is “rebuilding the way we operate at YC,” he said. “We now have an internal AI agent, for instance, named Stray Light that kind of has a personality, and then it has a company brain. Like it actually has the total context of every founder we’ve ever backed, anyone who’s ever emailed us, like all the applications.” Tan, who is, naturally, an avid lover of technology (as anyone running Silicon Valley’s famed startup accelerator would be), believes personal AI agents will eventually become mainstream, if one major problem is solved: Costs have got to come down. “It’s too expensive right now,” he said, adding that he knows the amount of money he spends on AI agents is “a crazy privilege that not everyone can do.” But freebie agents controlled by Big Tech maybe aren’t the answer, either. When discussing the future he’d like tech to build, and how Meta as a social media company has impacted us, he said, “This is a huge company that controls the algorithm, and we all wish that they didn’t at some level,” he said. “So you could imagine a personal AI that you control, that you program.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . events.title: U.S., Russia and Ukraine to resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week, Witkoff says
events.summary: The U.S., Russia and Ukraine will hold peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 in an effort to reach a breakthrough on a deal for ending the war. Why it matters: U.S. officials say the meeting to restart a diplomatic effort suspended in February due to the war in Iran is a result of talks Presidnt Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin in recent weeks. The White House hopes Putin will be more willing to compromise after Trump agreed to lift sanctions on Russian diesel sales and took other steps welcomed by Moscow. So far, Putin's only apparent concession is agreeing to resume talks. The parties remain far apart, particularly over territory. Russia's escalating attacks on Ukrainian cities and Putin's refusal to agree to a ceasefire casts doubt on prospects for progress. Zelensky said on Monday Ukraine has intelligence that Russia is preparing another massive attack against its energy and logistics facilities on Tuesday "when the world will be watching the American midterms". Driving the news: Kushner and Witkoff will lead to U.S. delegation for the talks in Abu Dhabi. "Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace," Witkoff said in a statement. Witkoff added that lower-level U.S. officials will meet this week in Brussels with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the EU, and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe's post-war security architecture, and economic opportunities to support Ukraine's reconstruction. "We look forward to building on the progress made in Kyiv, Oslo, and St. Petersburg toward a comprehensive, durable peace agreement that delivers lasting security for generations to come," Witkoff said.

events.title: British Airways lost my father’s vital life-saving machine
events.summary: He needs a dialysis machine to survive, but on a flight it was first damaged, then it was lost My father suffers from terminal renal failure and relies on a highly specific dialysis machine every night to survive. British Airways’ check-in staff twice insisted on checking this fragile 20kg lifeline into the aircraft hold where it was first damaged, then lost. When his outbound flight arrived at Heathrow, it was returned broken resulting in a frantic search for a loan unit and hours spent in A&E so my father’s blood could be monitored. On the return flight to Rome, the machine could not be found. My parents waited until 2am before being told to go home without the equipment that keeps my father alive. He had to borrow another unit from a hospital. His was finally delivered three days later with the protective case unsealed and critical internal components disconnected. The sheer terror and stress of missing a treatment, not knowing if the A&E could accommodate him in time, and fearing that his health had already been severely compromised, was indescribable. British Airways has missed all deadlines to address our complaint and is now ignoring our correspondence. DL , London Your father did not need to use the fragile unit during the flight but was concerned, rightly as it turned out, it might suffer damage in the hold. BA, in common with most airlines, allows vital medical equipment to travel for free along with its owner, provided it does not exceed the dimensions of cabin baggage. It’s essential for safety reasons that belongings can be stowed under a seat or an overhead locker. Your father’s device was too large, and I believe it was reasonable for BA to check it into the hold if the flight was full. If, however, there were spare seats, it could have allowed it to travel on one. It has since told you a seat could have been bought. The real shocker is that such vital kit was mishandled not once, but twice. The impact on your father could have been grave had loan units not been found. BA’s response was, at best, cavalier. When you wrote to me, a month had passed since your initial complaint and you’d heard nothing besides auto-generated acknowledgments. The company got its act together when I questioned its attitude. An operative called you to apologise and it managed, at last, to reply to your emails. However, you are unimpressed by its offer of £300 in e-vouchers to, in its words, “put things right”. I’ve suggested it convert this into cash and consider a sum that better reflects the impact on your father. It told me it will be in touch to discuss a “gesture”. events.title: Final polls, models and markets see a "blue tsunami"
events.summary: The threat of a blue tsunami is bearing down on President Trump's Washington, with virtually every major indicator forecasting a Democratic rout in Tuesday's elections. Why it matters: Expectations for the midterms have soared so high that some Democrats fear disappointment is inevitable, particularly if the party falls short of winning the Senate — a prize that seemed beyond reach just months ago. By the numbers: Five key metrics help distill the extraordinary consensus taking shape on the eve of the midterms. 🔮 95% and 80%: The probability of Democrats winning the House and Senate, respectively, according to election forecaster Nate Silver , whose model projects an average gain of 25 House seats. Silver says Democrats could now withstand a modest polling error and still capture the Senate — a remarkable cushion given the GOP's history of outperforming polls in the Trump era. 🗺️ 7 for 7: Democrats lead in every Senate battleground state surveyed in the final New York Times/Siena polls , including by 11 points in Michigan and seven in Texas. Trump carried six of those seven states in 2024, though five of the Democratic leads — Maine (+6), Kansas (+5), Ohio (+5), Alaska (+2) and Iowa (+1) — remain within the polls' margins of error. 🏛️ 240: The number of House seats Democrats could win under the upper end of Cook Political Report's forecast — potentially their largest majority since the first year of Barack Obama's presidency. Reaching that mark would require Democrats to sweep all 18 toss-up races. Cook already favors them in 222 districts, four more than needed for a majority. 🎲 73%: The probability of Democrats winning both chambers of Congress, according to Kalshi . After correctly favoring Trump in 2024, prediction markets have become a closely watched barometer of political expectations. Nearly $100 million in contracts have traded on Kalshi's congressional control market alone. 📊 +14: Democrats' lead on the generic congressional ballot in the final poll from AtlasIntel , which became the nation's highest-rated pollster after its remarkably accurate 2024 performance. Reality check: Even the pollsters forecasting a Democratic landslide are haunted by the possibility that they're still missing Trump voters. New York Times polling chief Nate Cohn warned that white Democrats were roughly 30% more likely than white Republicans to respond to the final Times/Siena surveys — a slightly wider gap than in 2020, when polls overstated Democratic support. Washington Post pollsters raised similar alarms after finding Democrat Adam Hamilton leading Republican Sen. Roger Marshall by nine points in Kansas, where registered Democrats were more than twice as likely as Republicans to participate. What they're saying: Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson have accused pollsters of deliberately manufacturing the appearance of a Democratic wave to suppress Republican turnout. "They're trying to create this idea of a blue wave and they're using the poll numbers to do it," Johnson said Monday , claiming conservatives distrust polling calls because they believe "it's a psyop." Between the lines: Prediction markets are sometimes touted as more accurate than polls because bettors have money at stake. But their odds often reflect the same polling data and political sentiment, leaving them vulnerable to the same blind spots. In Wisconsin, Kalshi gave state Rep. Francesca Hong a 96% chance of winning the Democratic gubernatorial primary the day before the August election. She lost to Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley. In Brazil, Kalshi gave Trump ally Flávio Bolsonaro an 84% chance of defeating President Lula ahead of last week's runoff. Lula won, prompting MAGA influencers to amplify baseless claims that the election was rigged. The bottom line: Voters will ultimately deliver the only verdict that counts. But on the eve of the election, the polls, forecasts and betting markets are all pointing in one direction.

events.title: Grab Holdings boosts 2026 forecasts on strong delivery, ride-hailing demand
events.summary: Sales will rise to US$4.15 billion (S$5.31 billion) to US$4.2 billion in 2026, Grab said on Nov 3. Grab raised 2026 revenue to US$4.15 billion-US$4.20 billion and EBITDA to US$790 million-US$800 million after strong ride-hailing and delivery demand. Its financial services unit posted its first core profit in Q3, as more drivers and merchants used loans, insurance and other products. Q3 revenue rose 27% to US$1.11 billion and monthly transacting users hit a record 57 million, even with high fuel costs and wider economic pressure. Grab Holdings raised its full-year revenue and profit forecasts after quarterly earnings beat estimates, signalling confidence that rising ride-hailing and food-delivery demand across South-east Asia will offset regulatory hurdles. Sales will rise to US$4.15 billion (S$5.31 billion) to US$4.2 billion in 2026 , while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) will be as much as US$800 million, the Singapore-based company said on Nov 3. In August, it had forecast sales of as much as US$4.15 billion and earnings on that basis of up to US$740 million. The stock rose about 2% in after-hours trading. Grab added about three million monthly users in the quarter through September for a total of 57 million, suggesting that it is succeeding in fending off intense competition from the likes of Indonesia’s GoTo Group. Demand for ride-hailing and food delivery is rising in South-east Asia as more people go online. Meanwhile, higher fuel prices are raising ride and delivery costs across the region of about 700 million people. Platform companies are offering incentives to drivers and customers to soften the blow, but that risks squeezing already thin margins. Regulators are also piling on pressure. Indonesia, one of Grab’s biggest markets, has already cut the maximum commission companies can charge on scooter rides, and is considering further rules in areas such as food delivery by the end of 2026 . Competition remains intense, with rivals such as GoTo and new entrants such as Green & Smart Mobility vying against Grab in populous markets like Indonesia and Vietnam. Uber Technologies, one of Grab’s backers, could also be a looming threat – its planned acquisition of Delivery Hero opens up a path for Uber Eats to re-enter South-east Asia. Alphabet’s Waymo also plans to launch robotaxis in Singapore in 2028 . The company, meanwhile, is striking deals to spur growth beyond its core business. In September, it agreed to acquire a majority stake in Singapore-based buy-now-pay-later and digital lending platform Atome Financial for US$1.49 billion, after buying US-based Stash Financial for an enterprise value of US$425 million. But not every deal has gone to plan. In October , Taiwan’s Fair Trade Commission blocked Grab’s roughly US$600 million purchase of foodpanda’s local delivery operations on antitrust concerns. In the latest quarter, adjusted Ebitda rose 74% to US$237 million, the company said. Analysts projected US$194.2 million on average, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. Revenue grew 27% to US$1.1 billion, roughly in line with estimates. To add users, the company has expanded its product offering to include more affordable and premium options. Grab is also expanding into games and microdramas, partnering other platforms to keep users on its app for longer. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Jason Low and Nathan Naidu said that despite its failed acquisition of foodpanda Taiwan, Grab is positioned to maintain its 2028 adjusted Ebitda guidance, given the roughly US$60 million the business would have contributed is small relative to its US$1.7 billion target. More details on Grab’s acquisition of Atome Financial could be disclosed at the earnings announcement. BLOOMBERG
